root_claims.title: Put cache lifetime in core
root_claims.choice: Export TurnScopedCacheScope and its typed handle from core. TypeScript still chooses when to begin a turn and release; core clears the entries.

root_claims.title: Keep six independent caches
root_claims.choice: One scope owns six separate typed handles: definitions, references, call targets, callers, callees, and position definitions. Each keeps its own Map.

root_claims.title: Return the exact cached value
root_claims.choice: Keep the existing identity and file-position keys. Cache values and promises without wrapping them. A stored undefined or empty array is still a hit; use Map.has.

root_claims.title: Keep two different failure paths
root_claims.choice: A returned promise stays cached even after rejection. A factory that throws before returning stores nothing, so the next lookup retries it.

root_claims.title: Start a turn after refresh succeeds
root_claims.choice: Keep the existing order: refresh source/project/workspace state, then clear all six caches. A failed refresh does not begin a new semantic-cache turn.

root_claims.title: Clear immediately; make release wait
root_claims.choice: Keep synchronous clearing before project release. Now the service and backend await project release, so its pending state and rejection reach the caller. The stack spec also asks for unchanged failure paths.

root_claims.title: Keep TypeScript's query work
root_claims.choice: Keep algorithms and miss observers in TypeScript. Cache reference/position locations, then rebuild reference projections and node arrays on access; those outward arrays and wrapper promises need not share cache identity.

root_claims.title: Accept files instead of a snapshot
root_claims.choice: Change the exported service's beginTurn input from WorkspaceSnapshot to readonly WorkspaceFile[]. The backend now passes snapshot.files; the service retains that file list.

root_claims.title: Compose a scope that can be reused
root_claims.choice: The service constructs a scope rather than extending a base. Handles expose getOrCreate only. Clearing retains handles and file inputs, cancels no promise, and permits new cache entries even while project release is pending.

root_claims.title: Add tests around preserved contracts
root_claims.choice: Add six TypeScript cases and four core cases for identities, empty results/rehydration, failures, clearing, failed refresh, awaited release, and old-promise settlement. Keep all five previous TypeScript tests and their assertions.

limit: Structural announcement check only. A human must still read every lower layer for semantic surprises.
